area.title: Main reason for import and additional details
area.scope: The main reason for import page with every reason, its hints and conditional reveals (internal market purpose, transhipment destination, transit exit point and destination, temporary admission exit date and point, re-entry), and the additional (animal) details page: certification purpose, unweaned animals and when the page applies. Stops at commodity details and identification.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.
claims.quote: Now we need to be really careful here because the prototype isn't accessible. It's not using some GDS stuff. It's using prototype thrown up by AI stuff. ... the prototype isn't necessarily production-grade with its solution.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam says the content of a search dropdown (such as which countries a country dropdown holds) is not settled by 'the frontend is correct' and may need more input.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: The reason for import page is at /import-reason and is reached from the overview task 'Main reason for import'; its title is 'Main reason for import - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.ref: trace T03 actions call@702, call@704 and title; T04 action call@877
claims.quote: Main reason for import - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The reason for import page has the caption 'About the consignment' and the heading 'Main reason for import'.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, span.govuk-caption-l and h1; T04 action call@881
claims.quote: About the consignment ... Main reason for import

claims.statement: The question 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' is the radio group's visually hidden legend, not a visible heading; the page heading 'Main reason for import' is what users see.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, legend.govuk-visually-hidden; T04 actions call@883 (group visible) and call@885 (no heading with that name)
claims.quote: <legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend govuk-visually-hidden"> What is the main reason for importing the animals? </legend>
claims.note: import-reason.spec.ts: 'if it is ever promoted back to an h1 this fails, mirroring the frontend fit spec.'

claims.statement: The first reason is 'Internal market' (submits internalMarket), with the hint 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'
claims.quote: Internal market ... For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).

claims.statement: The second reason is 'Transhipment or onward travel' (submits transhipmentOrOnwardTravel), with a hint about direct travel to a third country staying within the same port or airport.
claims.quote: Transhipment or onward travel ... For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.

claims.statement: The third reason is 'Transit' (submits transit), with a hint about entering Great Britain at one port or airport and leaving from a different one.
claims.quote: Transit ... For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.

claims.statement: The fourth reason is 'Re-entry' (submits reEntry), with the hint 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; it has no reveal.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, input#reasonForImport-4 (no aria-controls)
claims.quote: Re-entry ... For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.

claims.statement: The fifth reason is 'Temporary admission horses' (submits temporaryAdmissionHorses), with the hint 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
claims.quote: Temporary admission horses ... For horses authorised for temporary entry.

claims.statement: On a notification with no reason saved, no reason radio is selected when the page loads.
claims.ref: trace T05 action call@809 (Internal market not checked) and DOM at call@807 (no checked input); T03 action call@704
claims.quote: expect internal:role=radio[name="Internal market"s] to.be.checked NOT

claims.statement: Choosing Internal market reveals a nested question 'Purpose in the internal market' (a medium legend over radios) beneath it; the purpose is asked only under Internal market.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, div#conditional-reasonForImport; T07 actions call@1063, call@1065 (Breeding visible after choosing Internal market)
claims.quote: Purpose in the internal market

claims.statement: Purpose option 1 is 'Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift' (submits transfer-of-ownership-sale-gift), with a hint covering sales, purchases from a breeder or shop overseas and moves to a new owner with no sale such as a gift.
claims.quote: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift ... Any movement of an animal that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the animal from one person or entity to another. For example, animals that have been sold and are being moved to a new owner or will be sold once in Great Britain, purchases from a breeder/shop overseas and where an animal is being moved to a new owner with no sale involved (for example a gift).

claims.statement: Purpose option 2 is 'Transfer of ownership - Rescue' (submits transfer-of-ownership-rescue), with a hint about rehoming and adoption or fostering.
claims.quote: Transfer of ownership - Rescue ... Ownership of animal/s changes from one person or entity to another through rehoming and is adopted/fostered by new families, with or without an exchange or donation of money.

claims.statement: Purpose option 3 is 'Breeding' (submits breeding), with a hint about animals for reproduction.
claims.quote: Breeding ... Animals for reproduction. This includes animals intended to contribute to the genetic pool of a breeding program, improve livestock quality, or produce offspring.

claims.statement: Purpose option 4 is 'Research' (submits research), with the hint 'Animals for use in scientific or medical research.'
claims.quote: Research ... Animals for use in scientific or medical research.

claims.statement: Purpose option 5 is 'Racing, competition, show or training' (submits racing-competition-show-or-training), with the hint 'Animals to participate in competitive or training events.'
claims.quote: Racing, competition, show or training ... Animals to participate in competitive or training events.

claims.statement: Purpose option 6 is 'Approved premises or body' (submits approved-premises-or-body), with a hint about exhibitions, zoos, collections or conservation needing a licence or approval.
claims.quote: Approved premises or body ... Animals for exhibition, zoos, collections, or conservation programmes where a licence or approval is needed.

claims.statement: Purpose option 7 is 'Companion animal not for resale or rehoming' (submits companion-animal-not-for-resale-or-rehoming), with a hint about privately owned animals that cannot meet the non-commercial rules.
claims.quote: Companion animal not for resale or rehoming ... Privately owned animals being imported under the commercial rules as the animal is unable to meet the non-commercial requirements, for example, one or more animals being transported by a commercial transporter without their owner or an authorised person, owner that is not traveling within five days of the animals' movement or a group of five or more animals being accompanied by their owner.

claims.statement: Purpose option 8 is 'Production' (submits production), with a hint about animals farmed for meat, milk, eggs, wool or other products.
claims.quote: Production ... Animals that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.

claims.statement: Purpose option 9 is 'Slaughter' (submits slaughter), with a hint about slaughter shortly after arrival into Great Britain.
claims.quote: Slaughter ... Animals to be slaughtered and processed for meat production shortly after arrival into Great Britain.

claims.statement: Purpose option 10 is 'Fattening' (submits fattening), with the hint 'Animals to be fattened for meat production.'
claims.quote: Fattening ... Animals to be fattened for meat production.

claims.statement: Purpose option 11 is 'Restocking' (submits restocking), with a hint about replenishing populations such as game or fish.
claims.quote: Restocking ... To replenish or enhance populations of species, for example, restocking of game or fish.

claims.statement: When the purpose is first revealed, no purpose is pre-selected.
claims.ref: trace T07 action call@1067 (Breeding not checked)
claims.quote: expect internal:role=radio[name="Breeding"s] to.be.checked NOT

claims.ref: trace T07 request POST /import-reason 302 /additional-details; T03 action call@710
claims.quote: reasonForImport=internalMarket&purposeInInternalMarket=breeding

claims.ref: trace T08 request POST /import-reason 400 and actions call@1082, call@1086 (heading Main reason for import still visible)
claims.quote: There is a problem

claims.ref: trace T03 action call@744, .govuk-error-summary__list and p#purposeInInternalMarket-error; T08 action call@1084
claims.quote: Select a purpose in the internal market ... Error: Select a purpose in the internal market

claims.ref: trace T03 action call@744, title and input#reasonForImport checked aria-expanded=true
claims.quote: Error: Main reason for import - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.ref: trace T06 actions call@972 to call@976 and request POST /import-reason 302 /additional-details
claims.quote: reasonForImport=reEntry

claims.statement: Choosing Transhipment or onward travel reveals a 'Destination country' select (field transhipmentDestinationCountry).
claims.quote: <label class="govuk-label govuk-label--s" for="transhipmentDestinationCountry"> Destination country </label>

claims.note: These are plain govuk-select fields, not type-aheads, and keep the divider the origin list dropped.

claims.quote: <option value="">Select port of exit</option> <option value="" disabled="">──────────</option> <option value="GB DYC">Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC)</option>

claims.quote: Exit date ... For example, 27/3/2026 ... Port of exit

claims.statement: The exit date uses the MOJ date picker (moj-datepicker, a 'Choose date' toggle opening a calendar dialog with Select and Close buttons), which is outside govuk-frontend; the GOV.UK date input is the standard alternative.
claims.quote: <div class="moj-datepicker" data-module="moj-date-picker">

claims.ref: trace T03 actions call@708 to call@716; reason-purpose-scope.spec.ts comment
claims.quote: reason + purpose go in on one submit and the tail page completes the row.

claims.quote: leaving scope wiped the saved purpose, so no purpose radio is pre-selected and the task is owed again.

claims.quote: The purpose is owed again, and it is now enforced where it is asked: a blank save returns the page with the error rather than walking on.

claims.ref: trace T03 actions call@750 to call@762
claims.quote: Answering the newly owed purpose completes the row again.

claims.ref: trace T03 action call@738 (FR selected in transhipmentDestinationCountry and transitDestinationCountry; GB DYC selected in transitPortOfExit and temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit) and request POST /import-reason (concurrencyToken=7)
claims.quote: reasonForImport=internalMarket&transhipmentDestinationCountry=FR&transitPortOfExit=GB DYC&transitDestinationCountry=FR&temporaryAdmissionExitDate=&temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit=GB DYC

claims.statement: The reason page always posts reasonForImport plus every reveal's fields (purposeInInternalMarket when chosen, transhipmentDestinationCountry, transitPortOfExit, transitDestinationCountry, temporaryAdmissionExitDate, temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit), whichever reason is chosen.
claims.ref: trace T06 and T07 requests POST /import-reason
claims.quote: transhipmentDestinationCountry=&transitPortOfExit=&transitDestinationCountry=&reasonForImport=reEntry&temporaryAdmissionExitDate=&temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit=

claims.statement: The reason page has the same three exits as the origin page: 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview'; its Back link goes to the overview.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, div.govuk-button-group and back link href /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TAG440
claims.quote: Save and continue ... Save and return to overview ... Cancel and return to overview

claims.statement: The reason page is built from govuk-frontend radios with conditional reveals (one of them nesting a second radio group), govuk-select fields and the MOJ date picker.
claims.ref: trace T03 action call@704, class list of main
claims.quote: govuk-radios__conditional ... govuk-select ... moj-datepicker
claims.note: Nested conditional radios inside a conditional reveal go against GOV.UK design system guidance, which advises keeping conditional reveals simple.

claims.ref: trace T03 and T04 to T08: reasons chosen are only Internal market, Transit and Re-entry

claims.statement: Switching the reason from Internal market to Transit leaves the hidden purpose radio checked, so the Transit save still posts purposeInInternalMarket=breeding; the service discards it anyway, because on the next visit no purpose radio is pre-selected.
